name: Walther von Metz
credit: No portrait is known; a monogram is shown.
bio: Walther von Metz was a thirteenth-century minnesinger known from songs preserved in the Codex Manesse and from a mention in a poem by Reinmar von Brennenberg.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: The Flowers' Defect
poems.author: Walther von Metz
poems.text:
If the flowers we pluck this virtue had,
That they varied at their will,
Suiting men and women well or ill
As the wearer's heart was good or bad;

Women then men's nature might descry,
Men might judge of women too;
Then would all who were not pure and true,
Have to wear their wreath of flowers awry.

No such power, alas, do they possess!
All who please may pluck them now.
So with many a wreath that decks a brow
Rudeness, too, is shown and wantonness.
